thread.title: Review N13 installed receipt and executable identity driver

items.text:
Act as the review sub-agent for this task.

Independent read-only review. Current worktree /Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-dfe68040, HEAD79f7fe5f8428172924a34280a59f5a725ebe586e based on57cc38b0abb1c8dcb586d80f44455ab23a8f7a19. Review only current scripts/check-native-model-consumers.py and new scripts/test_native_model_receipts.py against HEAD, plus examples/native-model/README.md documentation. Never edit files/build/test/execute application code or spawn agents. Other agents draft apps only under excluded receipts; do not review unfinished drafts. Original task: actual installed 5-engine ModelCodec/Recorder/EvidenceRecorder independent bytes/config/phase/provenance/all25pairs/exact measured callback counts, source/executable identities and preserved lossless failures. Prior baseline review findings: TS application replay accidentally omitted counted provider so limits0 passed; driver never checked receiptcount dictionaries; executed Go/Swift/Rust binaries had no hashes. First resumed installed execution additionally failed before0 producers0pairs because Rust stamp regex collected both macros and engine IDs. Fix response: new strict canonical count validator for every producer/consumer using independent oracle constants (unchanged), capture-failure control flag required, file-valued runner args+interpreter/native executable SHA256/size before and after; engine-specific anchored compiler log regex independently compared to source/compiler expected stamp; isolated Cargo target to ensure engine build stamp emitted; 5 regression tests passed through Kyoto e735409f417f4d9ba30be8d177bf3d08. No library/golden changes. Evaluate false positives, missing identities, failure-path receipts, strictness and test coverage. Report actionable severity/path/line/scenario/fix or static clearance plus remaining execution gates. App negative controls/normalized field implementations are handled separately and will receive separate review; don't classify their current missing fields as driver regression. Do not make closure claims from static review.

I’ll review the three requested files against the stated baseline, focusing on receipt validation, identities, failure preservation, and regression coverage. I’ll keep this read-only and won’t run code or spawn agents.

The validator now enforces all ten counter names and exact integer values, including rejecting booleans. The Rust stamp matcher also excludes the macro crate’s prefix. I’m checking whether failure receipts retain enough evidence and whether the new tests cover the identity checks.

I found one gap in failure evidence: if a native runner is missing or unreadable during the final hash pass, collection stops and discards the accumulated post-run inventory. The regression tests cover receipt validation and stamp parsing, but not this path. The three reviewed files remained unchanged during review.

**P2 — Post-run identity evidence is lost when one executable cannot be hashed.** In [check-native-model-consumers.py:101](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-dfe68040/scripts/check-native-model-consumers.py:101), a missing or unreadable runner aborts `runner_snapshot()`, discarding its accumulated inventory. The failure handler at line 126 retries the same collection and records only `runner_identity_error`. For example, a deleted Go executable prevents retention of post-run identities for the surviving runners. The qualification still fails, but its failure evidence is incomplete.

Collect identities and errors independently per file, retain every available result, and mark identity verification failed when any entry cannot be verified. Add regression coverage for executable disappearance/read failure during both successful and failed command paths; the [current tests](/Users/jagatranvo/.t3/worktrees/stateless/t3-dfe68040/scripts/test_native_model_receipts.py:27) do not exercise identity collection.

Otherwise, the counter validator rejects missing/extra counters, incorrect values, and booleans; the anchored Rust matcher excludes macro-crate stamps while preserving independent stamp comparison. Handled command failures, timeouts, and receipt-validation failures retain raw logs and artifacts.

Reviewed against HEAD `79f7fe5f8428`; SHA256 prefixes remained unchanged:

- Driver: `751e745c2666c9ca`
- Tests: `558c7215e95b028f`
- README: `929c32d68dc47f3a`

No edits, builds, tests, application execution, or agents. Remaining gates: identity-failure regression coverage, separate application review, and fresh frozen-source Kyoto execution of five producers and all 25 pairs. The reported five passing tests do not establish installed qualification.
